originalTitle: SIF AUM jumps 29% to Rs 17,858 crore in June; inflows surge 171% MoM
simplifiedContent: Here's a simplified version of the news: Specialised Investment Funds (SIF) had a big increase in the amount of money they managed, with a 29% jump to Rs 17,858 crore in June. This happened because a lot more money flowed into these funds, with a 171% increase from the previous month. This is important because it shows that investors are putting more money into these types of funds, particularly Hybrid Long-Short Funds. The overall mutual fund industry also did well, with many investors continuing to participate. This suggests that individual investors, like you, are still interested in investing in the stock market, which is a positive sign.

originalTitle: DMart Q1 results: Cons PAT up 11% to Rs 860 crore, revenue rises to Rs 18,795 crore
simplifiedContent: Avenue Supermarts, the company that owns DMart, recently released its financial results for the first quarter of the year. The company made a profit of Rs 860 crore, which is 11% more than it made during the same time last year. Its total sales, or revenue, also increased by 14.9% to Rs 18,795 crore. This growth in profit and sales is a positive sign for the company, and its profitability, measured by EBITDA, increased by 15.4%. Overall, these results show that DMart performed well in the recent past, which may be good news for investors who own its stock.

originalTitle: Nearly 60% of foreign inflows into India-focused funds withdrawn since 2024 peak: Report
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: foreign investors have taken out almost 60% of the money they had put into funds that focus on India's stock market since the peak in 2024. This means they're no longer investing as much in India as they used to. The reason for this is that they're interested in investing in other areas, like artificial intelligence, around the world. As a result, $9 billion was withdrawn from India-focused funds in 2026, which is a significant amount. This shift in investment could affect India's stock market, and it's also interesting to note that investors are putting their money into other areas, like US stocks and even gold.

originalTitle: Nomura sees 22% upside in Ather Energy. Here's why it's the brokerage's top EV pick
simplifiedContent: A company called Nomura thinks that Ather Energy, a company that makes electric vehicles, will do very well and increase in value by 22%. They are telling their clients to buy shares of Ather Energy because they think it has a lot of potential for growth. The reason for this is that more and more people are expected to switch to electric vehicles, and Ather Energy is likely to benefit from this trend. Nomura has increased its target price for Ather Energy to ₹1,470, which means they think the company's shares will be worth that much in the future. This makes Ather Energy one of Nomura's top picks for investment in the electric vehicle industry.

originalTitle: Why large cap and mid cap funds could be the best mutual fund to bet on now, according to Abakkus study
simplifiedContent: A recent study by Abakkus Mutual Fund suggests that investing in large and mid-sized company funds might be a good idea right now. This is because these companies are expected to have better earnings, and their stock prices are currently reasonable. The market has recently gone down, which means it could be a good time to invest in these funds for the long-term. This is because the lower prices could eventually go up as the companies' earnings grow, making it a potentially good investment. The study thinks that now is a good time to invest in these funds because of the potential for stock prices to increase along with the companies' earnings.

originalTitle: AI chip fever returns? SK Hynix  share price surges 13% after blockbuster $26.5 billion US listing
simplifiedContent: SK Hynix, a company that makes computer chips, just listed its shares on the US stock market and raised a huge amount of money - $26.5 billion. The company's share price jumped 13% on its first day, which is a very strong start. This is surprising because the semiconductor industry has been a bit unstable lately, but investors are really interested in companies that make chips for artificial intelligence (AI). The high demand for AI technology is driving up the price of these chips, which is good news for companies like SK Hynix. This strong start suggests that investors are very optimistic about the company's future.
